In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8975):

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>`make verify-crd-schema` fails when run from a git worktree with:
>```
>Error: resolving comparison base "upstream/main": resolving revision "upstream/main": reference not found
>```
>
>The `crd-schema-check` tool uses go-git's `PlainOpen()`, which does not enable `commondir` support. In a git worktree, remote refs like `upstream/main` live in the shared common directory (the bare repo), not in the worktree's own ref space. Without `EnableDotGitCommonDir: true`, go-git only sees the worktree-local refs and cannot resolve remote references.
>
>The fix replaces `gogit.PlainOpen(repoRoot)` with `gogit.PlainOpenWithOptions(repoRoot, &gogit.PlainOpenOptions{EnableDotGitCommonDir: true})`. This is backward-compatible and works identically for normal (non-worktree) repositories.
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes [CNTRLPLANE-3824](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-3824)
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>Verified locally — `make verify-crd-schema` passes in a worktree after this change.
>
>## Checklist:
>- [x] Subject and description added to both, commit and PR.
>- [x] Relevant issues have been referenced.
>- [ ] This change includes docs.
>- [x] This change includes unit tests.

Let me output the final report. # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: `pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-aws-upgrade-hypershift-operator` - **Build ID**: `2075280849816784896` - **Target**: `e2e-aws-upgrade-hypershift-operator` - **Build Cluster**: `build01` - **Namespace**: `ci-op-n4b6k2qx` ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` "e2e-aws-upgrade-hypershift-operator" pod "e2e-aws-upgrade-hypershift-operator-hypershift-install" failed: pod pending for more than 1h0m0s: pod has not been scheduled in 1h0m0.001051748s 0/66 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 12 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 53 node(s) had untolerated taint(s). preemption: 0/66 nodes are available: 1 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 65 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling. ``` ### Summary The job failed during the **pre phase** because the `hypershift-install` CI step pod could not be scheduled on the `build01` CI cluster for over 1 hour. Out of ~66 nodes in the cluster, every single node was excluded: ~53 had untolerated taints, 12 didn't match the pod's node affinity/selector, and 1 was rejected by anti-affinity rules. Some events also showed "Insufficient memory" on the one remaining candidate node. This is a CI infrastructure resource exhaustion issue on the `build01` cluster, completely unrelated to the PR code changes.
Root Cause This is a **CI infrastructure scheduling failure**, not a product or test code bug. The `hypershift-install` step pod was unable to find any schedulable node on the `build01` CI cluster for the entire 1-hour timeout window. The scheduling breakdown across 106 FailedScheduling events consistently shows: - **~53 nodes** had **untolerated taints** — these nodes are reserved for other workloads or in maintenance and the CI step pod doesn't carry matching tolerations. - **12 nodes** didn't match the pod's **node affinity/selector** — the pod requires specific node labels (likely architecture or workload-type labels) that these nodes don't have. - **1 node** was rejected by **pod anti-affinity rules** — another pod with anti-affinity was already running on the only otherwise-eligible node. - **Up to 13 nodes** were transiently **unschedulable** (cordoned), further reducing the pool. - **8 events** specifically cite **"Insufficient memory"** on the one candidate node that passed all other filters, meaning even the last-resort node was overcommitted. The net result: 0 out of 66–81 nodes were available at any point during the 1-hour scheduling window. The CI cluster was under heavy resource pressure — notably, the lease acquisition for `hypershift-aws-quota-slice` itself took ~63 minutes (18:23 → 19:26), confirming cluster-wide contention. The PR ([CNTRLPLANE-3824](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-3824): Fix verify-crd-schema in git worktrees) only modifies CRD schema verification tooling and cannot cause CI cluster scheduling issues. This failure is not related to the PR changes.
Recommendations 1. **Re-trigger the job** — this is a transient CI infrastructure issue. A `/retest` should succeed once `build01` cluster pressure subsides. 2. **No code changes needed** — the failure is entirely in CI infrastructure pod scheduling, not in any product or test code. 3. **If retests keep failing** with the same scheduling error, escalate to the CI infrastructure team (OpenShift DPTP / Test Platform) — the `build01` cluster may need capacity expansion or taint/toleration review for CI workload pods.
